root_cause: The native image was assigned to the next JIT in the uploading task. libbpf cold memcg/name feature probes can issue BPF_PROG_LOAD between module arm and the intended stub load, consuming the image. The later stub then followed ordinary JIT emission of its return-zero bytecode. The global pending slot also allowed another task to replace the image.
source_trace: kprog/libnativeloader/src/native_loader.cpp:3321 upload_and_load_stub arms before load_stub_prog creates its tail-call probe map
vendor/libbpf/src/bpf.c:220 and228 map creation calls memlock and program-name feature probes
vendor/libbpf/src/bpf.c:329 program load probes program-name support
vendor/linux-framework/kernel/bpf/core.c prior bpf_native_image_take consumed the global pending image on owner == current
fix: BPF_F_NATIVE_IMAGE selects the intended load. Its task-owned pending image transfers to prog->aux before stock verification, and the architecture JIT takes that program image. Fork initializes a fresh pending slot; task/program teardown releases images. Bound native loads retain B verification and emit P directly, including when B has subprograms. Missing images or failed native emission return errors.
userspace: Both raw direct stub attr.prog_flags and trusted-worker opts.prog_flags select the native image through the shared wire constant.
regression_cases: cold libbpf feature probes and intervening ordinary load
replacement of the same task image
BPF-to-BPF subprogram B emits the bound native P
failed verifier load releases its image
fork isolates pending state and child teardown releases its image
parallel tasks retain their distinct native images
